newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign stake in India's BHEL rises.
newsitem.headline: Foreign stake in India's BHEL rises.

text.p: India's state-controlled power generation equipment maker Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) said on Wednesday that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) had increased their holding in the company to 16 percent.

"The foreign institutional holding has gone up to 16 percent in the company. The shares have not come for transfer, so I cannot say whether the FIIs are U.S. pension funds or not," BHEL's finance director K.G. Ramachandran told Reuters.
He was commenting on a report in the Economic Times newspaper that BHEL had become one of the first public-sector companies to attract the attention of U.S. pension funds as an investment stock.
The newspaper said that NYNEX Corp Master Pension Trust and another U.S. pension fund had picked up a stake in BHEL, boosting FII holdings by four percent.
The Indian government holds 67.7 percent of BHEL, Indian financial institutions hold 10 percent, employees hold one percent, and the rest is with the public, the newspaper said.

BHEL's net profit rose to 4.68 billion rupees ($ 131 million) in 1996/97 (April-March) from 3.5 billion in 1995/96. Its sales climbed to 57.4 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 48.33 billion rupees in 1995/96. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
